$comment: The declaration half of Sprint-0 Gate G2's outbound probe.
EVERY `request` STARTS null AND THAT IS THE POINT. This project's most
likely failure is implementing from text that was superseded; the version
of it that applies here is implementing from a REMEMBERED vendor endpoint.
A probe that runs against a path nobody read off the real account produces
a 404 that looks exactly like the capability being absent — and `absent` on
an mvp_required row is the finding that stops the MVP.
So: `source` must name where the path was read (the account's own API
reference, with its URL or screen), and the runner REFUSES to execute any
probe whose source is empty. Filling this file is a reading task against
the real panel, never a recall task.
`subject` records whose phone number the probe uses. E9 puts the stored
response body on a permanent clock, so it must never be a real consumer.

probes.question: Does a server-side API call ring the seller's leg and then the destination leg, end to end?
probes.source: Aloware panel -> Integrations -> Two-Legged Call API tab, read 2026-08-05. Path, field names and the body-token auth scheme are copied from that page's own example, not from memory.
probes.subject: [DESTINATION_E164] — supplied by the owner as a phone he answers himself. E9 requires a synthetic subject because this row is never purged; a real consumer here would acquire a permanent clock.
$notes: AUTH IS IN THE BODY. The panel's example puts api_token as a JSON field; there is no Authorization header. A Bearer assumption returns 401, which this gate would have read as `absent` on an mvp_required capability.
ring_group_id 29109 = Default Inbox, the one the Test Line routes to. The agent leg therefore rings the Aloware app rather than a second handset, so only ONE phone is needed.
line_id 63949 = 'Test Line' (+1 737 427 3994), a single-number line. Chosen over line 65123 so the dial cannot touch the 58-number Local Presence pool that carries production traffic.

The panel warns in its own words: 'Two-Legged Call API usage is considered automated & paid.' Each run of this probe places a billable call and rings two phones. It is never run without an explicit go-ahead.
line_phone_number is per call, which answers a Phase-2 open question: the two-legged path CAN present a per-seller caller ID rather than dialling from one shared line.

probes.question: Is there a GET that lists calls since a timestamp? ARR-INT-08's reconciliation backfill has no implementation without it.
Can a webhook destination be registered, and does the API report what is registered? If subscription is panel-only, that is itself the finding.
Can a contact be looked up by E.164? Dedupe is OURS either way — we never ask a third party who owns a lead.
probes.source: Aloware panel -> Integrations -> Contact Lookup API tab, read 2026-08-05. Path, parameter names and the query-string token placement are copied from that page's own cURL example.
probes.subject: 2025550100 — the North American reserved fictional range (555-0100..0199). Guaranteed not to belong to a person and guaranteed not to be in the account's contacts, which is what makes it a lawful subject for a row E9 never purges.
$notes: THIRD ENDPOINT, THIRD AUTH PLACEMENT: the token is a QUERY PARAMETER here, while two-legged takes it in the JSON body. There is no single scheme to assume.
That placement is exactly why request_url is redacted before it is stored: `api_token` matches SECRET_PARAM and the substituted value is matched too, so the permanent row holds [REDACTED].

EXPECTED OUTCOME IS 404 {"error":"Contact not found."} and that is a SUCCESSFUL run. A 404 in the documented shape proves the endpoint exists and the token was accepted; only a 401/403 would say otherwise. It is NOT evidence of `absent`.

It also cannot promote contact_lookup to `verified`: CAP003 requires a 2xx, and a 2xx here would mean a real consumer's record in a permanent row. Verifying this capability lawfully needs a synthetic contact that does not exist yet — creating one is an account change and is Jorge's call.
PRIMARY PURPOSE OF THIS RUN: prove the API token works, using a GET that costs nothing and rings no phone, before spending a billable dial against an account with an unpaid invoice.

probes.question: Does the SMS endpoint exist and answer? NOT to be fired until 10DLC status is known — an unregistered send is a compliance event, not a probe.

body.message: Sprint-0 Gate G2 test message. Reply STOP to opt out.

probes.source: Aloware panel -> Integrations -> SMS API tab, read 2026-08-05. Path, field names and the body-token placement copied from that page's own example.
probes.subject: [DESTINATION_E164] — a colleague of the owner. CONSENT BASIS: the owner states he notified the recipient in advance and authorised this send explicitly on 2026-08-05, after being told that this is a real TCPA-governed text from a 10DLC-registered business number and that E9 stores the response permanently. Recorded here because a consent basis that lives only in a chat log is not a consent basis.
$notes: THE 10DLC PRECONDITION IS SATISFIED: Business Registration, A2P Brand and A2P Campaigns all read Approved, so this send is carrier-legal. That was the gate on firing this probe at all.
`from` is the Test Line (+1 737 427 3994), never the 58-number Local Presence pool.

`user_id: 120776` is deliberate and is itself part of the measurement. The panel documents three behaviours: -1 sends as the company with no owner, omitting it sends as the contact owner, and a real id sends AS THAT USER. Per-seller attribution on SMS therefore exists at the API level — which the MCP surface notably cannot do.
The message stays under 160 characters (one segment) and carries opt-out language, because a real 10DLC-registered business number is sending it to a real handset.

DESTINATION_E164 is the only unresolved value and SPIKE014 refuses to send until it is filled. It must be a number the owner controls and consents to receive on: this is a real text under TCPA, and E9 stores the response body permanently.

WATCH FOR: whether a `to` that is not already a contact gets one created silently. Aloware does this on the MCP surface; if the REST SMS path does it too, it is a consent-ledger hazard worth recording.

probes.question: Does disenrolment exist? Enrolment is structurally unreachable until it does — sequenceEnroll() needs a DisenrollProof token only a verified disenroll can mint.
Probed for completeness only. Nothing in the MVP enrols.
